title: Apply evidence-backed lifecycle transitions, resolution, and reopening
summary: Implement domain projections separate from identity and attention. Ordinary recovery and reopening follow qualifying evidence automatically, with human decisions required only where the host assigns that authority.
implementation: Validate profile edge, scope, current assessment, matching evidence, and authority.
Commit transition plus downstream invalidation atomically against revisions and epoch.
Handle late-discovered resolution with separate effective and knowledge time.
Reopen on declared recurrence or invalid resolution while retaining old transition history.

acceptance.criterion: Only corresponding qualifying evidence resolves a condition.
acceptance.verification: Compare unrelated and matching success for two generic condition keys.

acceptance.criterion: New occurrence can reopen; old-event redelivery cannot.
acceptance.verification: Resolve, replay the original event, then add a distinct happening.

acceptance.criterion: Retraction weakens support without proving the opposite.
acceptance.verification: Retract sole resolution evidence and inspect profile-defined unknown/reopened state.

tests: Acknowledgement does not close the condition.
Ordinary recovery needs no user confirmation receipt.
risks: Coupling lifecycle to attention would close quiet matters and resurrect old warnings.

reuse.application: Adapt evidence/authority/outcome guards while leaving legal rules outside the core.
